text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures resumed their downward course of last week, drifting much of the Monday in negative territory in what traders described as dull trade. The market was on edge about details of the government's traditional New Year's Bund issue which will be made public on Tuesday and were unwilling to take aggressive positions ahead of a slew of German and U.S. economic data due later in the week. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.61, down 0.09 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts made back only some of the day's losses and ended lower across the curve. Traders said there is little chance the week's data releases will bring much comfort to the market and they expect conditions to grow even more volatile as the U.S. non-farm payroll looms. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-12/32, down 7/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settled little changed after a lacklustre session with most looking to the implications of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report for U.S. long-bond yields and the likely impact on European yields. The March contract survived early jitters, finding support at 127.76/80, and then traded within a narrow range to settle down 0.04 at 127.86.
ITALY - The Italian debt market was closed for a National Holiday. In after hours trading the Italian bond stood at 127.25 down 0.65.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened narrowly mixed on Monday, and are expected to stay in tight ranges until more information on the economy is known. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-14/32, down 4/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.75 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract was down by midday on Monday. Traders said the yen's weakness versus the dollar in the morning led to selling of JGBs. Talk that a Japanese television station had reported during the New Year break that the Bank of Japan may raise interest rates before April also may have depressed JGBs somewhat, traders said. But in after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 123.71. up 0.01 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - The Halifax Building Society topped a list of quality names in the primary market on Monday morning as the new year bond-issuing blitz got under way in earnest.
Investors can expect a barrage of new paper to be proffered in the coming days and weeks with borrowers of all hues said to be lining up a deal.
